I am Minishcap1! I've played League since 2010. I became a Singed one-trick in 2013 and have mained him ever since. I have achieved Challenger rating in seven separate seasons, with a peak rank of 44 on NA. 

The goal of this guide is to be an ongoing project that I can easily update with the most current Singed information on how to win with Singed.
column3:
Singed can use many keystones/runes well. It is possible to use runes situationally to react to individual games. However there will generally be 2-3 keystones that are superior to others in terms of overall usability. I will first go over the major keystones, and then follow up with more situational keystones.

Runes in GREEN = Standard/Major keystone options, Runes in BLUE = Situational/Optional
column4:
Updated For: Patch 25.23

With Riot removing AP from items and runes over the last 18 months, I have felt that higher AP builds are more important. Deathcap is a consistent item for me currently, because outside of Liandry's I feel like there is no better way to increase your damage output, and thus your solo carry potential. I still play lower-AP builds when my team has a lot of damage and needs frontline, but in general higher AP builds are more important than before.
column6:
Doran's Ring - Most stable starting item. Buy this vs most melee matchups. Provides good mix of stats. Starting with 2x health potions also gives the most possible sustain before first recall.

This start means you spend extra gold on a refillable potion, and extra gold on the 2 hp potions, so consider that you will be down 250 total gold compared to dark seal + refill, but you have better combat stats early game, which can help with lane.
column7:
Singed is one of the most versatile item users in the game. He has a huge number of options to build, so learning which items to build and when is key to success. 

For best current builds, see "Builds" section.

Generic item order when you don't know what to buy is Liandrys item 1 or 2 > Rylais item 1 or 2, depending on whether you need damage from Liandrys or CC from rylais. Then you go Deadman's 3, Bloodletter 4, Deathcap 5. You buy t2 boots either by rushing them first or finishing them after item 1 is complete. Besides Liandrys, most items are situational and I vary them often.

Singed's only true core item is Liandrys, everything else is situational.
column8:
Generally I only buy one tank/non-AP item per game but you can buy 2 tank items if you need to provide more frontline to your team. Remember that Singed is a Damage over time champion, which means that often simply living longer = more damage. However, not buying enough AP will cause your DPS to drop, even if you live longer.

As a general rule, f your team has a lot of damage but no frontline, then stack 2 tank items and play for the win, but NEVER buy 2 tank items if your team lacks damage.

Many games I will opt for a full AP build if my team has sufficient frontline and I am in a position to comfortably deal damage.
column9: Boots of Swiftness - Generically best boots on Singed. Movespeed synergizes with your passive + ult, and the slow resistance is good because you will always get focused as Singed. Buy these when enemy team comp has a mix of damage, cc, and AD/AP and you think that Mercs or Tabi will not excel in that game.

Dark Seal - Greedier starting item. You can buy this if you are confident in your matchup and early game skill. You save 150 gold compared to Doran's ring start because you start with refill and don't purchase 2x hp potions. Stats are good but not as good as Doran's ring. Lack of mana regen can hurt if you are not used to playing Singed and conserving mana early game.

Buy this when you are confident that you can use the +150 gold saved in order to secure a lead in top lane, or you are confident that enemy laner will not be able to punish you for having lower stats than Doran's ring start.
column7: Liandry's Torment - Singed's only true core item, purchased 1st or 2nd every game. Liandry's is your single biggest damage spike for the entire game, especially vs tanky champs. Generally I build Fated Ashes first, and then haunting guise second, since I value the waveclear, but you can build haunting guise 1st if you need to fight your enemy laner a lot.
column8: Deadman's Plate - Most Standard armor item for Singed, HP + MS + Slow resist + Armor, everything he needs except Damage. Solid 2nd or third item if enemy has fed physical damage. Never buy this before Liandry's, only after, or you will have ZERO waveclear. Worse than Zhonya's vs true damage, but cheaper + higher mobility.
column9: Mercury's Treads - Only buy this when the enemy team has a mix of Magic Damage + CC to the point where you can judge that it would be stupid to go Swifties or Tabis.

column4: Triumph, Legend alacrity, Last Stand, Nimbus, Celerity. Can take absorb life or Legend haste if you prefer those runes. Should take standard shards for highest early game AP, but can take Greedy if you're comfortable.
column6:
Boots - You can start boots + refill as the ultra-greedy starting option if you are VERY confident in your early game. You have no AP and no HP to start with, but you do save 150 gold on your refill and 300 gold on boots for a total of 450 gold saved. Buy this start ONLY when you are very confident that you will not lose farm or tempo in the early game (which is usually never going to be the case for 99% of games) but if you are a god/psycho you can make this start work for a good start.

Boots level 1 isn't that bad on Singed either, but you do lack combat stats/waveclear with this start until you recall.
column7:
Rylai's Crystal Scepter - Good stats, good slow effect. Low price. Makes you hard to gank since you perma cc anyone chasing you. Very good vs champs with no gap closers, such as Darius/Nasus and ADCs/enchanters. Lower damage than Liandrys, but provides you and your team with big value in the form of CC.

Buy this item 1 or 2 most games, but you can delay it until item 3 or 4 if you need other stats first. Singed is one of the best Rylai's users in the game. However, most games where my team has a lot of CC already, I skip this item depending on matchup and comps, because I think that Rylai's damage just doesn't scale that well for DPS.
column8: Jak'Sho - Very good item for mid-late game in terms of pure defensive power, but gives zero damage and is expensive for a tank item. Buy this only when you really need to frontline vs mixed damage (AD & AP) and buying more AP is not an option. The majority of this item's power is locked behind getting it fully charged up and getting the bonus resistances, so you are still vulnerable at the start of a fight to getting bursted since you don't have a reliable method to charge this before the start of a fight. The exception is if you have Liandrys + rocketbelt, you can use Liandry's from rocketbelt to start charging this up before you go in.
column9: Plated Steelcaps (Ninja Tabi) - Buy these when the enemy team has 3+ AD threats + autoattack threats, otherwise Swifties are better.

column6: Doran's Shield - I almost never start this item. It's main use is when you are trapped under turret vs a ranged top laner and can only last hit with auto-attacks. If you are in this position as Singed, you already lost IMO, so you should not look to buy this item unless it's a last resort IMO. I would rather skip a creep wave and run through jungle to look for a proxy instead of staying under turret to farm, while getting chipped for HP and eventually dove.
column7: Bloodletter's Curse - Best anti-MR item for Singed most of the time. If you are solo AP, then Cryptbloom or Void Staff are better, but you will very rarely be the solo magic damage threat for your team. Good stats, Good cost, but you need to have other damage items such as Liandry's for this item to be higher value.
column8: Unending Despair - Good mixed-resist item for a good price, but requires conqueror to gain full value IMO since the damage proc aids Conq stack generation. Is outscaled by Jaksho in terms of pure tankiness, but the lower cost, higher damage, and sustain make this a great Singed option if you need 1 item to give mixed resistances.
column9: Symbiotic Soles (Baron Boots) - Good option to splitpush with, but not as good  as they used to be since you now have to evolve them to gain the 4 second recall. Useful in games where your team is hard stomping the enemy, or where your team is getting hard-stomped in laning phase, because in both cases you can try to splitpush instead of group.

column3:
Tips: Conqueror is the most "standard" keystone choice on singed, since ability power is valuable on him for damage. I normally take this vs tanks in lane, but it is also playable vs most melee champions because they will be eating poison trail damage in trades/fights.

Poison gives 1 stack every 4 seconds

Standard conqueror combo is Poison > fling > auto. You can also get stacks with items like Rocketbelt and Unending Despair, both of which synergize well with this rune.

Proxying is fine with conqueror but be aware that your mobility is much lower so risk of death is higher. If you are ahead and enemy laner is playing safe, you can try to fight enemy jungler after you farm a proxy wave.
column6:
Cull - You can buy this item on 1st recall vs farming matchups, such as tanks top or easier bruisers/fighters (Maokai, Ornn, Sion, Mundo, etc) where you're going to be able to farm a lot. Don't buy this vs matchups where combat stats are more important. Do not buy this at the start of the game since you will have adaptive force AD which is bad for poison.

Cull is quite good on Singed to be able to generate extra income since if you are uncontested you should be able to farm a lot. Singed doesn't use the stats of this item but he can stack it quite fast. Good greedy option.
column7:
Rabadon's Deathcap - Very good 2/3/4/5th item on Singed. Synergizes with your ult to give extra AP on top of the normal amount. Poison trail AP scaling is good for Dcap and Fling hitting harder can help kill squishies as well. 

This item is more important to buy in the Season 15 meta because so much AP was lost throughout item nerfs + ult nerf, that having deathcap is the only way to deal big damage as the game goes later.
column8: Force of Nature - You can stack this with Deadman's plate for 2x tank + movespeed combo, but remember that buying two tank items will lower your damage. However if you need the defensive stats (Magic resistance, HP) from this item, and your team can provide damage, then it is a solid choice due to synergistic stats with Singed.
column9: Sorcerer's Shoes - I almost never buy these, but Season 15 is probably a better time to try them than ever before since AP was cut from almost every AP Bruiser item and damage is a commodity resource now. They may be good, but I need to experiment more before I recommend them.

Tips: Save your phase rush during trades/dont use it randomly when trading. Save it for when you need to actually disengage. Phase rush movement speed increases per level, cooldown decreases per level. 

Helpful to escape during proxy when you are ganked. In teamfights, can proc on frontline to zoom through backline. 

If you don't know what rune to take, Phase Rush is always safe.

Proc combos are: Poison > fling > auto, Poison > w > auto, Poison > auto >auto

Normally I buy this either 1st, or later into the game after I finish Liandrys and other items as a way to gain lower cooldowns in a high-action game (lots of fights)

You also can use this to reliably pop enemy spellshields, if you are unable to do it with W since W can be clunky.  Buy it when enemy team comp has many ranged champs and you cannot simply walk up to them to fling. Gives a conqueror stack as well as 1 out of 3 procs for phase rush.

column3:
Ghost + Flash - Most "standard" Singed summoner spell setup. In most elos, Singed is a bit less reliant on TP early game than most champs, since he can proxy a wave and recall behind enemy turret. This means that you can take Ghost + Flash in order to fully unlock his mobility for teamfights. This summoner setup is the strongest at teamfighting as well as the safest early game. I would recommend this setup to most Singed players, and beginner Singed players. Strongest pickoff potential on fed enemy carry due to flash + Fling combo.

Be careful about falling behind though, if the enemy top is good at blocking your proxy + reset, or if you are having trouble finding proxy due to enemy jungler pathing for top. This can lead to extended laning scenarios without TP, which can be hard, since you have to recall for resources at some point, since Singed has no built-in sustain. Also vulnerable to splitpushers in mid-late game since you need to be able to clear a wave behind them before rotating to a teamfight.
column6: Singed's itemization order is very versatile. The only true core item for him is Liandry's. Everything else is situational
column7: Standard build is just a general-purpose build that tries to do a bit of everything. If you don't know what do build you can generally fall back here. It's not always the best build but it should function okay vs most comps.
column8: AP-Heavy build focuses on solo carry potential. I tend to prefer high AP builds recently because Riot removed so much AP from Singed's core items, and runes. In order to deal meaningful damage, higher AP values are needed.
column9: Movespeed build is something I like to build when my team lacks engage, or when I am falling behind in a lane that is going poorly. The purpose of this build is to give ou the ability to make plays and be annoying when you don't have gold to buy standard items.

column3:
TP + Ghost/Flash - Teleport is great to help reset your lane early game, and great for Macro plays later into the game. Teleport helps play the map. You have less mobility in teamfights, but more pressure on the map/sidelane. Try to play more aggressively in fights when ghost/flash are up, and a bit more conservatively when it is down. Better pick vs splitpushers since TP helps play the map. 

TP + Ghost vs TP + Flash is up to comps, preference and comfort. If your team has no easy way to kill enemy carries, then flash gives you a gap close to catch them with fling. If enemy team has a lot of melee champs and you want a lower cooldown summoner, then ghost will excel. 

The hard part about this setup is you only have one mobility summoner, but the strong part is that you have a more stable sidelane and don't need to worry about being able to join your team from sidelane.

Ignite + Flash/Ghost - Generally I only take ignite when it's mandatory to try and get kills early vs a champ who will outscale you (Example: Kayle). Pair this rune with Conqueror or Summon Aery only, as those two runes help you to get kills during laning phase, where ignite is strongest.

However, there are many Singed players who run ignite every single game and have great success with it, regardless of matchup. It depends if you are comfortable playing an early-game focused singed or not. Ignite will generally get outscaled by other options, and is seen as an early snowballing option when you need to be offensive.

column4:
Singed tends to get outscaled in a pure 1v1 scenario vs dedicated fighters but outscales almost every top laner in terms of 5v5, assuming you are not super behind and your team is not hard inting.

In general, you either rush full T2 boots, or your 1st item. T2 boots rush, esp swifties, is never bad on Singed but you lack waveclear rushing them. However vs ranged champs, Movespeed is important so you get harassed less and can get in range a bit more.
column6: This Matchup section is written with the perspective of playing vs Challenger / GM players. At lower elos, you will be able to succeed more often vs the harder matchups because enemy players will not be able to pilot their characters perfectly. However, the matchup tips are still relevant for every elo.
column7: You can swap your starting items, runes, and summoner spells based on your preference when you are more experienced on Singed. I wrote these with newer and less experienced players in mind, but also I try to present my logic for taking what I take.

column8: Matchup Tips

Focus on dodging his Q sweet spots. Use phase rush right before or right after he lands W on you in order to disengage the slow-cage. Grievous wounds helps shut him down in teamfights. You can actually solo kill him at 6 if you all-in him when he's close to your turret. He has good spacing to fight you in the open of the lane, so focus on proxying unless you are getting a gank or all-inning him near your turret.

column7: Doran's Ring + 2 Potion or Dark Seal + Refill
column8: Akali bullies you hard until level 6, and then can easily all-in you. Early game, walk up to the wave to bait her to Q the wave and push it. If she hits Q, she will back off to activate her passive. Just stay away until she uses it. Her level 6 is stronger than yours. Rush Negatron Cloak and focus on surviving and scaling. You outscale her in 5v5.

If running conqueror, trade with him HARD early levels but back off before you die. His HP is worth more than yours because you can push and recall. Play around waves and tempo. If running Spellbook, focus on crashing the wave safely and proxying with Hexflash. If you cannot crash safely, then skip a wave and just start proxying. Scale for 5v5

Her Q cooldown is long early-game so you can bully her a bit, but you lose every 1V1 after 1st recall because she scales EXTREMELY hard with AD and ability haste, so after 1st recall focus on farming and scaling for 5v5. If she ults you, try and land W under your feet and kite away. You lose short trades and all-ins after she buys AD and CDR so just focus on farming to scale for 5v5.

Treat it similar to other ranged matchups where you look for very aggressive early trades with conqueror to drain her HP bar when you reset. Once she gets mana+CDR she is much more annoying, but you can all-in her at 6 and win if she is close to your turret. Otherwise just focus on farming until she pushes up, but proxying is okay too.

You can trade early with conqueror and win. You can potentially look for solo kills pre-1st recall if you make good trades. After sheen the matchup swings in her favor, but its still playable as long as you don't lose tempo and don't feed her. Focus on dodging her W and E2, and farm your 1st item spike. You outscale her in 5v5 and use teleport to stop her splitpush. You can predict where her E1 will land on the wall and put your W down and she will get stuck there.

He is lane dominant with Grasp + E and Silence. If he has Hail of Blades, he scales worse but is much deadlier in 1v1. Just rush your Liandrys ASAP while farming and play for 5v5 because you cannot kill him 1v1 unless he is stupidly pushed up. Stay away from him as soon as you are below 60% hp because he can easily kill you, unless you are confident you can dodge his Q and W, tank the E without dying to R.

column7: Doran's Ring + 2 Potion or Doran's Shield
column8: NEVER APPROACH DARIUS LEVEL 1. Never approach Darius without phase rush available. Never approach Darius without Fling available. Follow these rules and rush Rylais. If you somehow get ahead, you can go Liandrys instead. He can EASILY run you down and kill you if you slip up even a little. Scale for 5v5 where you are stronger than him.

Mundo can farm pretty well against Singed and Singed has trouble solo killing him after 1st recall, so this matchup can be annoying. Stay away from his Qs, hide behind minions, chunk him by popping his passive with your fling, and you can fight/trade with conqueror stacks. Rush Liandrys ASAP and use teleport to stop his splitpush. Deathcap rush is decent since Mundo doesn't build early MR as much anymore.

Let her push first few waves to build a bounce off of your turret. You don't win early trades. When wave bounces, hard push into her turret and proxy. You can rush Rylais or Liandrys depending on how ahead you are. Don't use your E unless her W is down or you are confident she won't use it. This matchup has Fling versus Riposte mindgames, but you cannot win long trades. You can use your W on your feet + poison + auto to activate phase rush as well if she saves her W. Focus on scaling for 5v5 and use your TP to answer splitpush

Hard Matchup. He has complete prio on the wave level 1 unless he messes up his barrel. Every time his passive is up, you lose the trade. Bounce off of your turret and focus on proxying and scaling for 5v5. You can never get in range to fling unless you pop Ghost or Flash, unless you outplay the barrel or your jungler has CC.

Garen is an easier version of Darius. Same rules, don't approach without fling/phase rush. You can however contest him at level 1 as long as you don't tank his entire E. You can build Liandrys or whichever item you want against him. you can solo kill him with Conqueror as long as his ignite is down, but Phase Rush is better vs him most of the time. Don't drop low because his ignite + ult will kill you from like half hp. You beat him in 5v5s but he is stronger in sidelane.

Vs mini-gnar on 1st 3 waves, you can build a crash by trading aggressively, and chunking his HP bar. Proxy and reset. He beats you after 1st recall, but you beat him at 6. It's easier to fight Mega Gnar than mini gnar. Let mega gnar push up to your turret, dodge his W and fling him under your turret for an all-in. Otherwise, just look to push, proxy and scale. A good gnar knows how to kite you so Rush tier 2 boots, most likely Swifties.

Easy matchup until he buys mana+CDR, at which point he can literally E + W trade on you 3 times before your fling is up twice, meaning he can perma lock you and kill you. Only way out of this death combo is Phase Rush. Other than that the matchup isn't too bad, just trade farm and outscale him for 5v5. 1st item Liandrys or Rylais are both fine. Early merc treads or negatron cloak really cut his damage. In a long fight you can kill him assuming you get multiple flings before he runs to his turret. Be careful near his turret because he can ult you into it and then Q and E you.

I prefer Phase rush in this matchup, but you can play conqueror to trade harder with her early game. You can solo kill her at 6 as well, but she needs to be near your turret. The longer the game goes, the stronger she gets. She hard outscales you in 1v1 but you outscale her for 5v5.

He has push prio, wins trades, wins all-ins, can poke you, kite you, one-shot you, etc. Only way this lane is playable is if your jungler hard camps your lane and even then you have to flash over the wall to force proxy. Honestly just dodge this matchup or pick a different champ.

Rush chain vest ASAP because you will turn it into deadman's item 2. You need armor to survive. Focus on dodging E. If you get hit by E, run away and kite out the tentacles. Her R cancels your fling. You can outscale her for 5v5 and make yourself hard for her to kill. Chain vest into Swifties into Liandrys into DMP.

Skill matchup. She has early game wave prio with her passive + conqueror. You can win trades if she misses her E tho. Focus on dodging E. You can gimp her with your W as well, when she ults just throw W on her instantly. Rush Liandry's because Rylai's won't help if there are minions nearby.

Don't use your fling until after he uses Q, otherwise he will insta-Q back onto you for his E stun. You win long trades before he gets Sheen. After sheen he wins long trades. You can all-in him at 6 if he is close to your turret. He hard outscales you in the sidelane so your job is just to stop his splitpush and look for good 5v5 fights. I rush Liandry's but you can go Rylais if enemy team has a lot of divers.

Same idea as most ranged matchups, either trade super hard early, crash wave and proxy. Or skip wave and go proxy. Try to not get trapped under your turret because you will get poked. You can rush chain vest and become a lot harder for him to kill you. Or if you get ahead just rush Rylais or Liandry's and run him down. You win level 6 all-in if he's close to your turret, but otherwise this matchup is Jayce favored. Scale for 5v5.

Singed can almost never solo kill K'sante while Ksante has multiple windows to kill Singed during laning phase. Just focus on farming and proxying to scale for 5v5 as you will never kill Ksante 1v1 unless he massively fucks up. In teamfights you can ground him with W after he ults a teammate, and then focus on peeling him. Rush Liandry's and then situational.

Kayle will beat you in short trades and all-in until level 3 when you can put 2 points into Q, and even then it's close. If you want to look for solo kills, take ignite, otherwise you can pressure her 1v1 with non-ignite setups but killing her becomes hard at 6 due to her becoming ranged and her ult. If she is ever pushed up to your turret, and you have ult + ghost, you should all-in her instantly and look for the kill. You should build heavy AP during mid-late game to keep trying to kill her. She is way stronger than you 1v1 in late game but you can win in a good 5v5. Rush Rylais if you can snowball vs her to try for multiple kills.

Rush negatron cloak vs AP kennen. You can slow push and crash 1st 2 waves into a 3rd wave proxy and execute. Focus on farming up for teamfights because it's very hard to solo kill kennen unless he uses E on the wave, while pushing up to your turret, and you have a summoner. You can make yourself very hard for him to kill with MR rushing but in general this is a hard matchup that's kennen favored.

Kled has the highest base HP in the game when mounted, so rush Liandry's almost every single time. He will win long trades pre-6 because of his re-mount mechanic. However post-6 if you are able to dodge his Q and goo-fling during his dash, you can kill him. Very hard to kill once he has Ravenous Hydra. Singed has a better time vs Kled in teamfights where you can W him as soon as his ult lands to stop a lot of his mobility. His dismount and dismounted Q will both cancel your fling's CC so play around that in mind. Your W cancels his dismounted Q's dash but not the damage.

He can easily poke and gap you with his Q and Comet, but he has a hard time all-inning you unless you eat way too much poke before recalling or proxy-executing. You won't solo kill him unless you can take a favorable long trade near your turret. Farm and scale for 5v5, rushing Liandrys. In teamfights, you can cuck him hard if you W him right before he ults. After he ults, you can run into the clump to peel with W and E. Do not get hit by his ult because you can die fast during the CC and tenacity does not reduce knockup duration.

Easy matchup besides his base damage and grasp. You win long trades. Singed Q does not charge up Maokai passive so he naturally heals less vs you than other AP champs. He does have good waveclear so it's hard to choke him out for CS, but he should have very little kill pressure on you, and you should scale for 5v5. Rush Liandrys.

This matchup feels like it should be easy but it is not. Mordekaiser has a lot of base damage and is manaless with a shield + heal, so he will win short trades and long trades for the most part. However, you can solo kill him if you can fling him under your turret when his passive is up to poke with a turret shot. Try to not use your W until after he ults so you can goo fling him inside of his R and run away. I would say it's important to save your ult until after he ults, but tbh he does so much base damage that it doesn't matter most of the time. You win 5v5 vs him generally. QSS no longer works vs his ult.

You don't beat him in trades due to his sustain, so Push hard, crash waves, and attack his turret plates. You can stop him from recalling with W so try and keep him under his turret for as long as you can. Once he gets sheen, he wins trades hard and you can't attack plates anymore, so look to scale by farming. Nasus dumpsters you 1v1 but you are very good vs him in teamfights. Rylais helps peel him off of your team and Phase Rush is used to run away when he withers you.
Rylais rush or Movespeed Build. If he hits Q he will run you down until he is OOM or you die. Can only play the matchup once you finish rylais, or Aether Wisp + Moonplate if going Movespeed build.

Phase rush is mandatory in this matchup. You cannot get level 1 prio. Focus on dodging his axes and never walk up without phase rush available. Cosmic drive is very good in this matchup to have more ults and more kiting. You can win 1v1s before he finishes Ravenous hydra if you kite while fighting. After he finishes Hydra, 1v1 is much harder. You outscale in 5v5s but not 1v1.

Ornn deals a lot of damage in trades, but should have a hard time stopping you from farming and scaling. You can look for 1v1 kills via all-in if he is close to your turret. You can gain prio on 1st 3 waves and proxy+reset. If he uses W on you before you are in melee range, BACK OFF so he can't proc the brittle. You can sometimes fling him right after his W and right before his auto lands to cancel the auto, but the timing can be hard. You can fling hmi back when he dashes. You can fling him as he's about to hit his R ram to knock up. The easier way to deal with his R ram is to put W on him, as it cancels his ability to dash into his R. Ornn should generally be free outside of the early levels being hard. Rush Liandrys and Bloodletter's.

Play this lane defensively on 1st 3 waves and bounce off your turret for crash. You definitely outscale him in 5v5 but eventually when you get armor you can 1v1 him as well. You can optionally rush chain vest for early tankiness vs him. You can rush Liandrys or Rylais depending on enemy comp. I generally prefer Liandry's. Conqueror setup is aimed at having more damage for trades, Aftershock is all about surviving his burst combo. Spellbook is just a utility focused setup to farm around him. He will bully you early game but once you have armor and level 6 you can start to farm a lot more aggressively, and even look to all-in if he's close to your turret. Don't be afraid to pop your ult to farm.

She has good poke with Q and passive, but you can get prio on 1st 3 waves and look for crash + proxy. If she builds bruiser poppy, she will deal good damage in 1v1s. Tank poppy will deal less damage but be very hard to kill. However, you do outscale her for teamfights and you outscale her 1v1 as well. This matchup shouldn't be too hard. Remember that her mana costs are very low so if you spend too much mana you will OOM a lot faster than her. Stay away from walls as poppy will ALWAYS look for a stun angle on you. Otherwise you should be fine. Conqueror for damage is better but Phase Rush is playable if enemy team has a lot of slows. Rush Liandry's.

Hard matchup. Play very aggressively early to poke her healthbar and threaten with conqueror stacks + ignite. Look to crash the wave and reset ASAP. She will also have ignite and be able to kill you if the trades aren't great. You can rush chain vest and pair it with Tabi/Steelcaps if her team has multiple AD threats. After you crash wave and proxy, spam ping your jungler for ganks. Your jungler NEEDS to camp a quinn lane, otherwise she will eventually poke you down and kill you, or roam easily to mid/bot and kill them because singed pushes turrets slowly without Deathcap. Matchup is playable with jungle camp, but hard without. TBH i would perma ban this rat champ if I didn't think urgot was 10x worse to play against than her. Consider dodge.

Easiest matchup of your life. If rammus is pressuring you as singed in any capacity, please consider replacing your Leauge install with educational pattern recognition games for kids. He has no way to pressure you 1v1, outside of you getting taunted into his turret. Singed doesn't build attack speed or AD so his W his useless against you. He can escape easily with powerball but he can never stop you from free farmign the entire game. Honestly, just buy a cull and enjoy the free matchup. It's hard to solo kill him but just get perfect CS and scale for teamfights while listening to a podcast or something. Only way you lose is if your team gets hard diffed. Liandrys into bloodletter's.

Renekton will out-trade you before first recall so let him push towards your turret, and look for turret flings, as he will walk up to try and hit you with Q and W. If you get chunked too hard, just recall and reset with TP. Don't let him dive you. If you manage to hit him with turret shots, you can look to all-in. In general, renekton is a lane bully who you will eventually outsscale for teamfights, and potentially for 1v1 if the game goes long enough. He continues to scale a lot more than he used to, champs in league tend to not drop off a cliff as much as they did in older seasons. However, assuming you can farm evenly wihout falling behind, you can perform well in the game for teamfight phase. He will have general lane dominnace over you, but if youa re able to play well you can still find your farm and proxy and be somewhat okay. However, if renekton gets ahead he will STEAMROLL you, so don't let that happen. Liandry's rush, but Rylais is okay if you have less gold.

Do not walk in the bushes at level 1. Instead, try and drag the 1st wave towards the river so he has a harder time setting up his bush jumps. You can W a bush that he's in to prevent his bush jumps. Rengar has superirority in short trades, and in sustain. However, you do outscale him 1v1 and for teamfights especially, as long as you don't feed him kills. He will eventually get Ravenous Hydra, at which point you should be proxying anyways. He will have prio on 1st 3 waves but if you play it well you can actually crash and look for proxy. This matchup is not as bad as it seems once you get the hang of playing around his bush leaps. Liandrys rush is fine. Rush chain vest or tabi if you are willin to delay your damage to make it a LOT harder for him to kill you.

Riven will take ignite, so remember to play around that. Riven always has prio on 1st 3 waves and a good Riven will look to poke you hard with Q level 1, so give up wave prio if you have to.  She can 100-0 you at level 2 and 3 with her conqueror + ignite + abilities combo. Bone plating is helpful in this matchup. Chain vest or Tabi rush can be helpful as well. Eventually at 6 you can play a bit more confidently to look for farm and proxy, but Riven will always look to try and kill you, so be aware. Riven can also easily counter-proxy you. Assuming you are both even in farm, Riven will beat you 1v1, but you should perform better in 5v5. If riven is having a hard time killing you, she will look to roam into mid or into your jungle to kill your teammates, so ward up and ping if you think she's going. Not the easiest matchup but it's playable. You can fling her out of her Q3. You can also W onto yourself when she E's forward to stop her from doing her Q combo. I tend to rush Liandrys.

Treat him like the AP version of Renekton. He has early prio and wins trades, but rumble also has good poke. However at 6, you can all-in him if he's close to your turret. If he overheats, BACK OFF of melee range. You can rush Negatron cloak or merc treads, or both depending on enemy comp. You outscale for 5v5 but he can 100-0 you EASILY if you are caught out with no MR. Phase rush is what I prefer in this matchup but conqueror is fine if enemy team has other melee champs that you can fight in 5v5s.

You can get wave prio because his early poke is not too bad. Ryze will run phase rush but you can look to trade really aggressively level 1 and 2 to burn his HP down while you crash the wave. Negatron rush or Merc treads rush is fine here. I prefer Rylais rush against ryze becuase he has a hard time escaping once his phase rush is spent. You can all-in if he's pushed up to your turret at level 6. Your W grounding stops him from teleporting away with his ult. You can also fling him during his ult's activation to prevent the TP away. Ryze gets quite strong as he scales and will generally be able to deal with you 1v1 unless you are able to engage on him from a bush. Like most ranged tops, you will outscale in 5v5 but ryze is quite a strong teamfighter. He can also splitpush with his R and TP, so be aware that you will have to answer that.

Sett isn't too bad but he can snowball on you if he gets ahead. Early armor is really good against him. You can buffer fling during his E pull to get out of his range. You will actually win long trades in this matchup. If he has ignite, play more carefully. His ult + full combo is dangerous and can burst you from very high hp. Always try to dodge his Center-W. He can cancel your Fling with his R, but you can prevent him from ulting with your W. In general Sett is a fun matchup. I rush Liandry's.

Shen out-trades Singed for the entire laning phase, when building AD or Tank. However, his waveclear is trash until he gets tiamat or Hollow Radiance. Use this to your advantage to focus on crashing waves and proxying. At 6, you proxy while keeping an eye on him to stop his ult with your W or E. Sometimes it's more beneficial to let him TP out and just take turret plates/Turret FB. Unless your team is full AP and he stacks full MR, you can 1v1 him post-laning phase and win if you need to, but its better to save your ult for teamfights. Focus on your macro in this matchup. You outscale him for 5v5 as well. Shen is most dangerous in the early game. Rush Liandry's.

Like most tanks, he is good at trading into you early. However he will have a hard time stopping you from farming. You can look for solo kills on him if he ever overcommits to a wave or over-extends. Try to stay in front of him so he cannot ult away. You can gain early prio in this lane to crash and proxy, or you can try to look for solo kills near your turret. Sion does scale *extremely* well in terms of pure tankiness, but you do pump much more damage than him in a 5v5. You generally cannot solo kill him after laning phase, his HP bar is just way too big especialyl with resistances, but keep maintaining your macro and shine in 5v5s. Rush Liandry's.

Sylas will out-trade you early but after first recall you have much better waveclear than him and can focus on your macro. Don't take long trades against him because he will out-heal your with his W. He can steal Singed ult and Singed ult is VERY good for Sylas, so be careful of that for teamfights. In an all-in from full hp, you should win if he is near your turret. Otherwise just keep your cs high and outscale him for 5v5. Eventually you beat him 1v1 as well. I rush Liandry's but Rylais is fine too.

One of the harder tank matchups because his damage and CC is just really good versus single-target, so in top lane 1v1 he shines. Just don't get stunned near his turret because he will eat you and then spit you under his turret, and then knock you up and kill you. Focus on dodging his Q. You can only kill him if you all in him near your turret, otherwise just focus on your CSing and macro because he is hard asf to kill. Rush Liandrys and you outscale him hard for 5v5, and eventually you can also kill him 1v1 but it might not be worth your ult cooldown during teamfight phase.

You can play agressively early to chunk his HP but teemo can actually kill you on the first wave if you are not careful, because his single target damage is really good early game. Skip waves to proxy if you have to. If you take spellbook or inspo secondary you can just flash the wall to proxy faster, and then use hexflash after recall. You can even hexflash into enemy base to just cause chaos because there's not many good options vs teemo. If you can get to 6 without being down CS and not giving kills, you can all-in him near your turret. You can rush rylais or whichever item you prefer, just depends on the game. Buy sweeper at level 5/6 and start sweeping his shrooms. He can put shrooms in jungle entrance and exits to deny proxy, so be aware. Your jungler NEEDS to camp for you. Be annoying with your pings to try and get ganks. TBH this matchup is dodgeworthy for Singed, but can be played if you are willing to accept tilting levels of pain.

We take teleport in this matchup because trundle's entire purpose in the game is to just push sidelane as hard as he can, no matter what, because even if he dies he wants to just hostage you in side lane so you can't go teamfight, which is what singed wants to do. Teleport helps mitigate and answer his splitpush. Phase rush to disengage his trade/all in. Don't walk up without your fling. Don't walk up without your phase rush. His ult hard counters yours, but you still gain the movespeed/AP/regen from it. He steals your armor and MR. You lose short and long trades, you lose all-ins, but you teamfight so much better than trundle. After laning phase, call another teammate to answer trundle so you can go teamfight. Otherwise, if your team is losing, its kind of GG because he takes 1 or more turrets every time you leave to teamfight. Annoying matchup that not nerfed only because his pick rate is low. Rush Liandrys, but you can rush Rylais if you take conqueror (not recommended for newbies). Zhonyas is good against trundle for when he ults you. Deathcap can actually let you win fights later on if you somehow get to that point.

Less annoying version of garen only because his burst damage at 6 is weaker. Otherwise follow the same principles. Don't walk up without fling or phase rush both. Focus on farm. Rylais cucks tryndamere but is lower damage. Liandry's can kill him after his ult, but it's less forgiving than Rylais. You can play conqueror in this matchup if you are good at Singed and are comfortable in the matchup. TP is to answer his splitpush. Overall tryndamere is not that bad, just another split pusher who coinflips games, but you can consistently solo kill him if you get ahead by just stat checking him and kiting him during his ult so he can't crit you as much. Trynd has prio on first few waves due to his high AD and crit-RNG, so just let him push and bounce off your turret while looking for turret flings. He has a sustain advantagebut you should actually win all-ins as singed vs him. I rush rylais but Liandrys is fine, just less forgiving.

Honestly just dodge this matchup until they nerf it into the ground. Urgot is my current permaban. This champ is so hilariously overpowered that the only reason it's not nerfed is because Urgot is threatening to release the Epstein Files on Riot. He beats you in short trades. He beats you in long trades. He beats you in all-in. He beats you after laning phase. He doesn't outscale you in 5v5 but you will have so little gold that he will just easily statcheck you and run the game over. He can zone you, he can cancel your fling, he can fuck your mom, there's nothing Urgot can't do against Singed. PERMABAN IT. 

If you have to play vs it, just rush warden's mail + tabi and pray that your team wins the coinflip, otherwise it is GG because you can never do shit against this champ if he rubs his 2 braincells together to produce an electrical impulse.

Same idea as other ranged matchups, just play aggressive early to chunk her hp bar and crash wave, reset and try to kill her when it bounces. Vayne is more vulnerable to ganks because of how squishy she is, butif your jungler doesnt take the easy ganks then she can hard outscale you 1v1 and turn into a menace. I prefer high AP items like Liandrys into Zhonyas to just have as much damage as possible. Deathcap later on is good too. You absolutely outscale her in 5v5 but 1v1 is where she will try to always win the game. Think of Vayne like a ranged version of riven, except she has a much worse early game. Winnable, but spam ping your jungler for help. Setup ganks near your turret, but if jungler ignores you, you can all-in only if she's near your turret.

Vladimir is quite weak pre-6 and pre-1st recall, so use that time to your advantage to gain prio on the wave, crash, proxy and farm hard. Rush t2 boots because he is ranged. You can all-in him when he is close to your turret. Your ult cuts his healing so use that to your advantage. He can cancel your fling with his pool. You can predict that he predicts your fling by pooling, and just run on top of his pool to fling him afterwards. He can hold his E to extend his red Q duration. Stay away when he has red Q. Hide behind minions for his E. You have early wave clear advantage but he has more waveclear after a few recalls. Vlad scales quite well for 5v5 but should lose 1v1 to you in sidelane if you catch him alone and you are full HP. I rush rylais but you can rush Liandrys.

Once he bites you once, just stay away otherwise he will drain tank you. Volibear maintains prio on the early waves because of his thunder passive. He is also going to dumpster you in short trades. He wins long trades if you stay in melee range. At level 6 just treat every single trade as an all-in and farm with your ult.  Volibear is quite a strong lane bully against singed but he's not too bad once you have an item or two. I like Liandry's rush, but that can make it extremely hard to disengage him unless you are experienced on singed. Inexperienced singed should rush Rylais IMO.  He can be bursted in teamfights, where you should be performing. Fling him away from your team. His ult cancels your fling. Movespeed is good vs him as well. Use your W intelligently to proc phase rush and get away.

Annoying cheese pick matchup. Just don't focus on trading with him other than to use it as a way to access the creep wave. Focus on farming and proxying because you will NEVER beat him 1v1. He has too much healing and will easily turn the fight with barrier or ult. He can cancel your fling by holding his Q, so just save it until afterwards to disengage him. Never start a trade with fling or he will just kill you from 100-0. Warwick needs to bait you into fighting him for him to get ahead gold-wise so just don't fucking fight him other than to push waves. He can chase you with his W, so Rylais is a decent 1st item, or Liandry's if your team is winning. I cannot stress enough how much you should just not fight warwick 1v1, it is never worth it. Just scale up for 5v5 where you outperform him. His splitpushing isn't amazing either.

Pretty standard fighter matchup where you shouldn't have too much trouble as long as you watch your HP and get some early armor. I like Liandry's rush but you can do Rylais if you are learning. He can cancel your fling with his clone. Your poison reveals him with a shimmer during his stealth. Kite away during his ult and do not stand in it because you will get merked. His Q shreds your armor, so again just kite away. You can kill him in an all-in if he's close to your turret. He will have trouble stopping your proxy. Once he gets sheen, his trades are stronger, so be careful. Wukong shouldn't give you much trouble as Singed, and you can teamfight better than he can, even though wukong is quite strong in teamfights. You eventually do beat him 1v1, surprisingly, you just need to make sure you have enough AP to pump DPS because he will have sundered sky to heal.

Easier version of Yone. Poke his passive shield off with an auto or poison before you fling him. Your W stops him from using E or ult. you can fling him as he knocks you up with e+q to stop him from ulting. He can beat you during all-ins because of lethal tempo, but come online faster than he does since he has expensive items and needs a lot of gold. TBH singed kind of counters yasuo in 5v5 as well, but he can block your W with his windwall. You can fling him off of your backline, and just shit on him with poison + kiting. However, yasuo does scale like a demon and can always turn a fight with the right characters getting knocked up, so never get complacent even though this should be in your favor. I rush Liandry's.

Harder version of Yasuo. He can cancel your fling with his Q-dash. He can cancel your fling by recalling his E. He can win trades with his W shield. He wins all-ins with his E unless you take good trades and have high AP. Armor is okay early game but every other auto he deals magic damage, so be aware that it's not foolproof. I like to rush Rylais to cuck him during his E, but Liandry's is good too if you get ahead. TBH low-elo yones shouldn't be a problem, but high elo yone is very annoying to play vs. As long as you don't die to him and farm you should be fine, but just don't solo die to him otherwise he can pop off. You can fling him if he ults you point blank to reposition his character as well. Peel him off your back line in 5v5s and try to cuck his dashes with your W. You can actually trap him on your W at the end of his E duration, preventing his recall, and bait him into bad positions. Overall this matchup is Yone favored. It's playable, but annoying.

We take teleport to answer splitpush. Conqueror is taken because he trades really hard with ghouls, even harder with maiden. Put your focus on dodging his E. Ghouls can withstand a few seconds of poison, just kite them out to prevent autos, it's not worth right clicking them generally unless you save more HP that way. If he traps you in W, carefull right click it to auto it and break it. Legend alacrity is almost mandatory in this matchup due to his cage. At 6, he gains a lot of sustain and damage and splitpush due to his maiden. You can however fling maiden under your turret if he's pushing and try to kill her instead of him. It's worth it to ult to kill the maiden if you can. You beat him 1v1 if his maiden is on cooldown. Look to scale and proxy and farm for 5v5. His splitpush is annoying, but since you can beat him 1v1 even though he's annoying. it's playable. I rush Liandry's but rylais can cuck the ghouls and trap maiden for you to kill her. Maiden has a huge cooldown so bully her.

Zac has great base damage and sustain. He will take conqueror to generate AP during trades. He has pretty strong all-in. Try and step on his blobs to cancel out some healing. at level 6, ult to farm if you need to. You generally do outscale zac in 1v1 and 5v5, but he has many tools to disengage and run away. His engage power in 5v5 is also a lot better than yours, so he is good at 5v5 as well. Overall not the worst matchup, just annoying. Liandry's rush. Your ult also gives grievous wounds for healcut, so use it to your advantage. Your W blocks his E jump. You cannot prevent him from ulting because he is unstoppable during it.
